_about: Editorial review of data/influence_candidates.json, batch 1 (17 Nov 2026): fossil fuel, tobacco, mining, opioid, and the flagged family and finance senders. A kept entry names the kinds of influence its sentence states, a one-line summary in the atlas voice, and whether the tie ended or met protest. A drop says why. Batch 2 (17 Nov 2026): BMW, Hyundai Motor, Chanel. Candidates not listed here are not reviewed yet and are not shown. check "record" means checked against the record text, not yet against the source page. Batch 3 (17 Nov 2026): Sony Pictures Entertainment at LACMA, the one tie where a record links a funder’s lobbying and political giving to a space (entries may carry links: [{measure, text, source}]). Batch 4 (17 Nov 2026): BP at the British Museum, the Days of the Dead evening (2015) and the Scythians breakfast (2017); measure 'other' is lobbying of a government outside the US and the EU, named in `gov`. Batch 5 (17 Nov 2026): BP and UK ministers at the Science Museum, British Museum and National Portrait Gallery (2015, Art Not Oil FOI releases); Philip Morris at the Met and BAM against the 1994 Vallone bill (Truth Tobacco Industry Documents). Batch 6 (17 Nov 2026): UK government hospitality returns naming BP or Bloomberg as host at a space (British Museum, Royal Opera House, National Portrait Gallery, Serpentine, Tate Britain): hospitality, not the subject of any request. Batch 7 (17 Nov 2026): the Commons Register of Members' Financial Interests (via TheyWorkForYou's copy), BP at the Royal Opera House and JTI at the British Museum and the Royal Academy: hospitality to MPs at a space. Batch 8 (17 Nov 2026): two new spaces, Opera Queensland and Queensland Museum, with Queensland ministerial diary entries (Rio Tinto 2013; Shell and its QGC business 2018, 2019) and Shell QGC's $10.25 million to the museum since 2015. Batch 9 (17 Nov 2026): four funders added to the pilot (BHP, Morgan Stanley, Santos, LVMH) with their ties, and their contacts with government at a space (BHP at Queensland Museum, 2014 and 2015; Morgan Stanley and the Prime Minister at the British Museum, 2017). Batch 10 (17 Nov 2026): six new spaces (Glyndebourne, Brisbane Festival, State Library of Queensland, Cadogan Hall, Griffin Museum of Science and Industry, Meridian Hall) with their ties and contacts with government. Batch 11 (17 Nov 2026): four more spaces (Joyce Theater, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Perth Festival, WA Museum Boola Bardip) with their funder ties.

_about_checks: Checked against source pages, 17 Nov 2026: every page the entries cite was fetched once by an honest automated reader (1,151 pages, 1,083 read, PDFs as text). An entry is source checked when a page it cites names the funder and states the claim: automatically when every amount it gives sits beside the funder’s name on the page, or when it only says the funder is listed and the page lists it (in its text or, for a logo, in the image’s alt text or file name); otherwise by reading the page, with the excerpt kept as checked_quote. Partly checked: the page gives the tie but not one detail, named in checked_missing. Three entries the pages contradicted were corrected to what the page says, with the old wording kept in corrected. Not found: the pages cited do not state it, most often because the page that would (an annual report, a donor list) was not among the cited pages or could not be read; those entries stay as checked against the museum’s page in this atlas. Second pass, 17 Nov 2026: the entries not found on their cited pages were searched for on the web (annual reports, donor pages, the funder’s own releases, reputable press); a page that bears one out is linked as checked_source and added to the entry’s sources as extra_sources, checked_beyond_record marking it. Some cited files the first pass could not read (government hospitality spreadsheets, the Art Not Oil report) were read this time. Wikipedia alone, or a return that names a guest without the title the entry gives, counts only as partly checked.
